after.name: Question 1
after.problem: A $2\times 3$ matrix $A$ maps the unit sphere ${x\,|\,‖x‖=1}$ from ${R}^{3}$ onto an ellipse in ${R}^{2}.$ Given that the eigenvalues of ${A}^{T}A$ are $10,$ $7,$ and $0,$ find the length of the ellipse's semi-major axis.
after.worked_solution:
The matrix $A$ maps the unit sphere ${x\,|\,‖x‖=1}$ from ${R}^{3}$ onto the ellipse ${Ax\,|\,‖x‖=1}$ in ${R}^{2}.$

First, let's re-write the squared distance from the origin to the point $Ax$ on our ellipse, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖Ax{‖}^{2} & =(Ax)^{T}(Ax) \\  & =({x}^{T}\,{A}^{T})(Ax) \\  & ={x}^{T}\,({A}^{T}\,A)x,\end{aligned}
$$

  

where ${x}^{T}({A}^{T}A)x$ is the quadratic form with the matrix ${A}^{T}A.$ 

The maximum value of this quadratic form, when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of the matrix ${A}^{T}A.$

Since the largest eigenvalue of ${A}^{T}A$ is $10,$ we obtain

$$
{max}_{‖x‖=1}{‖Ax{‖}^{2}}=10\,⟹\,{max}_{‖x‖=1}{‖Ax‖}=\sqrt{10}.
$$

 

Therefore, the semi-major axis of our ellipse is $\sqrt{10}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14105204/assets/63d5de8c08559ecc88b4fd7e2184204a1e6ea2f8a9e8ca6af7959e2354876e3f.png)

A $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ maps the unit circle ${x\,|\,‖x‖=1}$ from ${R}^{2}$ onto an ellipse in ${R}^{2}.$ The corresponding ellipse and its principal axes are depicted in the diagram above. Given that ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are unit eigenvectors of ${A}^{T}A,$ which of the following is an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $9$ of ${A}^{T}A?$
content.worked_solution:
Suppose $A$ is an $m\times n$ matrix. Let 

$$
{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\,…,{v}_{n}}
$$

be an *orthonormal* basis of ${R}^{n}$ consisting of the eigenvectors of ${A}^{T}A$ with corresponding eigenvalues 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}\ge {\lambda }_{2}\ge …\ge {\lambda }_{n}.
$$

Then,

- ${\sigma }_{1}=\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}$ is the length of $A{v}_{1},$

- ${\sigma }_{2}=\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}$ is the length of $A{v}_{2},$

- $⋯$

In our example, we see that

- $||A{v}_{1}||=5={\sigma }_{1},$ which means that ${\lambda }_{1}={5}^{2}=25,$ and

- $||A{v}_{2}||=3={\sigma }_{2},$ which means that ${\lambda }_{2}={3}^{2}=9.$

Therefore, an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=9$ of ${A}^{T}A$ is ${v}_{2}.$

{v1,v2…,vn} be an orthonormal basis of Rn consisting of the eigenvectors of ATA with corresponding eigenvalues

λ1≥λ2≥…≥λn.

Then,

  • σ1=λ1 is the length of Av1,

  • σ2=λ2 is the length of Av2,

  • ⋯

In our example, we see that

  • ||Av1||=5=σ1, which means that λ1=52=25, and

  • ||Av2||=3=σ2, which means that λ2=32=9.
